messages:
pagerbot: 🔔 PagerDuty: HIGH - HTTP 5xx rate spike detected for service=ingress-edge-prod (threshold: 1.5% -> 6.8%)
incident-bot: auto-page fired to #incidents, routing to oncall: maria (oncall)
maria (oncall): looking now, thanks. any customer-facing alerts?
dan: seeing the spike in edge->proxy responses around 17:20 UTC. most are 502s, a lot of short-lived bursts. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/ingress/edge-errors?from=1704200000&to=1704200500
kevin: correlating with a spike in non-prod traffic from a partner IP range -- could be misrouted QA traffic hitting prod route. I'm pulling flow logs.
kevin: log snippet:
```
17:20:12 ingress-edge svc: upstream response=502 path=/v1/generate tenant=beta-partner-42 latency_ms=12
17:20:12 ingress-edge svc: upstream response=502 path=/v1/generate tenant=internal-e2e-qa latency_ms=11
17:20:13 ingress-edge svc: upstream response=502 path=/v1/embeddings tenant=beta-partner-42 latency_ms=9
```
maria (oncall): hmm. if that's QA traffic we should mute alert or narrow the scope. what do runbooks say?
incident-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ingress-5xx-spike

maria (oncall): triage plan: 1) quick assess customer impact 2) if non-prod origin, add temporary filter and mute PD threshold 3) if prod traffic, fallback to secondary region
dan: customer impact check: error-rate by customer shows top affected tenant is beta-partner-42 (error-rate 18%), but top enterprise tenants show <0.2% errors. so isolated.
kevin: confirmed source CIDR 198.51.100.0/24 belongs to partner QA infra. Looks like a misconfigured VPN that started sending test traffic to prod edge.
maria (oncall): ok, recommend we add a temporary ingress ACL to drop that CIDR and mute PD alerts for the next 30m. will also notify partner.
dan: command I'll run (routing admin):
```
# add temporary deny rule
redwoodctl routing acl add --cidr 198.51.100.0/24 --action deny --scope ingress-edge-prod --reason "temp block: QA traffic hitting prod"
```
kevin: +1 run it. also adding a bypass to avoid coldstart noise if we drop them.
(maria ran the command)
pagerbot: action logged: routing ACL added by maria (oncall) for 198.51.100.0/24 -> deny.
incident-bot: PD alert auto-muted by maria (oncall) for 30m (reason: known noisy non-prod CIDR).
maria (oncall): monitoring metrics...
(2m later)
dan: error-rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.4% in the last 3 minutes. top-customer errors are back to normal.
maria (oncall): good. sending quick note to partner ops: "Partner ops — we saw QA IPs hit prod edge causing 502 spike; we blocked 198.51.100.0/24 temporarily. Please confirm and correct routing. Contact: oncall@m.redwood.com"
kevin: leaving a sticky note in the partner ticket + tag legal/compliance if they require a postmortem.
maria (oncall): handoff: I'll stay for 20 more minutes then hand to @sre-rotation for follow-up. next steps for follow-up: 1) ensure partner has root cause fix 2) remove temporary ACL only after partner confirms 3) review alerts to add CIDR exclusion or tighten tenant-based alerting
sre-rotation: acked and taking over at 17:45 UTC. thanks for the quick mitigation.
incident-bot: note: no customer-facing incidents opened. recommended: file an internal blameless post with timeline if partner escalation occurs.
maria (oncall): marking this thread resolved -> will close PD incident after handoff. :white_check_mark:
